q: Break that down by product and channel.

checks.what: tool: reuses prior scope (drilldown or same window)

answer:
High-level: the week-on-week decline is concentrated in paid social and shopping channels — Instagram and Facebook together fell ~63% each and Google Shopping collapsed — while unattributed sales stayed flat. This shows the volume loss came from ad-driven channels rather than organic/attributed holdouts.

What changed (by channel, order-date basis)
- Instagram feed: ₹2,95,842 → ₹1,07,704 (2026-10-05..10-11 → 2026-10-12..10-16), −63.6% — largest single drop in sales and orders (161 → 53).  
- Facebook feed: ₹61,714 → ₹22,833, −63.0% — similar proportional decline to Instagram, indicating paid‑social pullback.  
- Google Shopping: ₹20,341 → ₹1,673, −91.8% — near disappearance of Shopping revenue; a strong contributor to the total fall.  
- Google Performance Max & Search: PMax ₹64,373 → ₹43,704 (−32.1%); Search ₹57,679 → ₹40,062 (−30.5%) — smaller but material drops in search channels.  
- Unattributed: ₹32,615 → ₹32,854, +0.7% — effectively flat, so non‑attributed/organic demand held up.  
- WhatsApp and a few minor channels: present in prior week (₹8,787 for WhatsApp) but not attributed in the current partial week — effectively 0 in the reported window.

Why it matters
- Paid channels that drove most volume (IG, FB, Shopping) reduced delivery or budget, which explains most of the aggregate sales and order loss; steady unattributed sales imply product demand still exists off‑ads.  
- Because today’s window (2026-10-12..10-16) is partial through 16 Oct, totals may rise slightly as data finalises, but the channel pattern is clear.

Unverified / missing: product-level breakdown was not run (need product net sales (P&L basis) or product net revenue); I haven’t yet confirmed campaign-level pauses or ad spend by channel for the same windows.
